note: Research batch 4 (microbial + cleaning depth) for ChatGPT to plug into data.js. Every PMID verified against the NCBI E-utilities API (titles and years match). Each study tagged with plant (oilIds), terpenes (compoundIds), uses (categories). Merge rule: skip any study whose pubmedId already exists in data.js.

studies.title: Evaluation of Antibacterial Activity in Some Algerian Essential Oils and Selection of Thymus vulgaris as a Potential Biofilm and Quorum Sensing Inhibitor Against Pseudomonas aeruginosa
studies.authors: Mohammed Aggad FZ, Ilias F, Elghali F, et al.
studies.finding: Thyme oil rich in thymol inhibited biofilm formation and quorum-sensing virulence factors in a hospital Pseudomonas aeruginosa strain, with docking data suggesting thymol and carvacrol bind its quorum-sensing receptors.

studies.title: Antibacterial and anti-biofilm activities of thyme oil, oregano oil, and their combination against Klebsiella pneumoniae and Acinetobacter baumannii polymicrobial biofilms
studies.authors: Anees TMM, Suchithra KV, Shetty AV, et al.
studies.finding: Thyme and oregano oils acted synergistically to disrupt dual-species Klebsiella pneumoniae and Acinetobacter baumannii biofilms by over 90%, downregulating biofilm-associated genes.

studies.title: Essential oils of Pinus sylvestris, Citrus limon and Origanum vulgare exhibit high bactericidal and anti-biofilm activities against Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Streptococcus suis
studies.authors: Jurado P, Uruen C, Martinez S, et al.
studies.finding: Scots pine and lemon oils showed strong bactericidal and biofilm-dispersal activity against multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae, attributed to alpha/beta-pinene and limonene acting on the bacterial outer membrane.

studies.title: Innovative antifungal strategies: enhanced biofilm inhibition of Candida albicans by a modified tea tree oil formulation
studies.authors: Tuan DA, Uyen PVN, Khuon NV, et al.
studies.finding: Tea tree oil inhibited Candida albicans biofilm formation but could not eradicate more than 50 percent of mature biofilm at the concentrations tested.

studies.title: Antibiofilm efficacy of tea tree oil and of its main component terpinen-4-ol against Candida albicans
studies.authors: Francisconi RS, Huacho PMM, Tonon CC, et al.
studies.finding: Tea tree oil and terpinen-4-ol interfered with Candida albicans biofilm formation in a 60-second rinse simulation, supporting potential use in oral candidiasis.

studies.title: In vitro antiviral activity of Melaleuca alternifolia essential oil
studies.authors: Garozzo A, Timpanaro R, Bisignano B, et al.
studies.finding: Tea tree oil and terpinen-4-ol inhibited influenza A H1N1 replication below cytotoxic doses, with no virucidal activity and no effect on the other viruses tested.
studies.limitations: In-vitro; influenza only among the viruses screened.

studies.title: Screening of the essential oil effects on human H1N1 influenza virus infection: an in vitro study in MDCK cells
studies.authors: Najar B, Nardi V, Stincarelli MA, et al.
studies.finding: Among 19 oils screened, eucalyptus and rosemary oils showed anti-H1N1 activity with low cytotoxicity, with eucalyptol correlating positively with cell viability.

studies.title: Virucidal Activity of Lemon Essential Oil against Feline Calicivirus Used as Surrogate for Norovirus
studies.authors: Pellegrini F, Camero M, Catella C, et al.
studies.finding: Lemon essential oil significantly reduced feline calicivirus infectivity, a cultivable surrogate for human norovirus, suggesting surface-sanitizing potential.
studies.limitations: Surrogate virus in-vitro; not tested against human norovirus.

studies.title: Antiviral efficacy and mechanisms of action of oregano essential oil and its primary component carvacrol against murine norovirus
studies.authors: Gilling DH, Kitajima M, Torrey JR, et al.
studies.finding: Carvacrol inactivated murine norovirus within one hour by disrupting the viral capsid, outperforming oregano oil and suggesting use as a surface sanitizer.
studies.limitations: Surrogate virus in-vitro; high concentrations required.

studies.title: Antifungal activity of volatile compounds generated by essential oils against fungi commonly causing deterioration of bakery products
studies.authors: Guynot ME, Ramos AJ, Seto L, et al.
studies.finding: Vapours of cinnamon, clove, lemongrass, and thyme oils completely inhibited bakery-spoilage molds including Aspergillus and Penicillium species.
studies.limitations: Vapour-phase lab model; efficacy dropped in real food matrices.

studies.title: Highly Durable Antibacterial Properties of Cellulosic Fabric via beta-Cyclodextrin/Essential Oils Inclusion Complex
studies.authors: Farouk A, Sharaf S, Refaie R, et al.
studies.finding: Cotton fabric treated with cyclodextrin-encapsulated lavender, lemon, and rosemary oils retained antibacterial activity through multiple wash cycles.
studies.limitations: Textile-finishing lab study; no worn-garment testing.

studies.title: Antibacterial activity and interactions of plant essential oil combinations against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria
studies.authors: Semeniuc CA, Pop CR, Rotar AM, et al.
studies.finding: NULL/MIXED RESULT: parsley and lovage oils showed no inhibition against any tested bacteria, and most thyme-oil combinations were antagonistic rather than synergistic.

newOils.name: Scots Pine
newOils.description: Steam-distilled from needles and twigs. Rich in alpha- and beta-pinene; studied for bactericidal and biofilm-dispersal activity.
newOils.safety: For external use; can irritate sensitive skin undiluted.
